doc.title: Clyde Kerr Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006

chapter: The future of New Orleans music
title: Declining politics; choosing his battles
summary: Asked if he'd go into politics, he declines because of his temperament and high blood pressure.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Maybe you ought to get into politics, you’ve got a lot to say.

No, see with politics, see my nature man, I know myself, I want to be cool, I want to be relaxed and all that so either I’m going to be like this or there’s the other side. There’s no in between. So if I’m going to deal with some of that other things man, I don’t know whether I’d like to. So I’ve tried that, I already have high blood pressure and take a lot of medication. I don’t need to deal with the politics. Someone else can do that.
Okay. Well after all you’ve done you deserve to take it easy and choose your gigs as you say.
That’s right. Exactly. Choose my battles.
